classes.title: Side effect lost after the commit
classes.signature: A row is written, then an alert, email, event or webhook is sent outside that write. A transient failure or a crash between the two loses the send for good: the next pass sees the row and skips.
classes.question: If the process dies, or the send fails, right after the database commit — what sends it again, and what stops it being sent twice?

classes.title: Check-then-write race between instances
classes.signature: Two replicas, cron passes or handlers read the same state, both decide, both write. Nothing makes the read and the write atomic, so one overwrites, duplicates or clears the other.
classes.question: Two instances run this at the same time on the same rows: what does each one read, which write wins, and is the check atomic with the write?

classes.title: Replayed or out-of-order event trusted
classes.signature: A handler acts on the fields of the event it received. The same event redelivered, a late one, or one older than the stored state, makes it repeat or undo work.
classes.question: This event arrives twice, late, or after a newer one: does the handler decide from the stored state, or from the event in hand?

classes.title: Unindexed or unbounded query
classes.signature: A new predicate has no index behind it, fetches the whole history and filters in memory, or runs once per item of a loop.
classes.question: Which index serves this predicate, how many rows does it touch when the table is 100× larger, and does it run once per item of a loop?

classes.title: Money passed through a float
classes.signature: An amount travels from storage to output through a JS number — Number(), parseFloat, arithmetic on number — and loses cents beyond 2^53 or to rounding.
classes.question: Can any amount pass through a JS number (Number(), parseFloat, + on number) between storage and output?

check.message: An amount converted to a JS number — keep it bigint or decimal text end to end.

classes.title: The same fact rendered twice disagrees
classes.signature: Two outputs show the same fact — PDF and CSV, a summary and its table, the screen and the export — through two code paths. A fix lands in one and not the other.
classes.question: Which other output shows this same fact? Does it go through the same function, and does a test assert that the two agree?

classes.title: Feature not wired end to end
classes.signature: Each layer works in its own tests, but the value the FR names never reaches the person: a producer omits a field, a page keeps old copy, a test injects the value the real path never sets.
classes.question: Follow the value from where it is produced to the screen or message the FR names: is every hop populated on the real path, not one a test injects?

classes.title: Tenant scope left to the caller
classes.signature: A query reads or writes rows of one tenant but the owner predicate lives in a caller's earlier check. A new caller, or a race, crosses tenants.
classes.question: Is the owner's scope inside this very query, or does it rely on a check made earlier by the caller?

classes.title: Calendar date read as an instant
classes.signature: A YYYY-MM-DD value is parsed as midnight UTC and shown in a negative-offset zone as the day before, or an instant is cut to a date in the wrong zone.
classes.question: Is this value a calendar date or an instant — parsed in which zone, shown in which?

classes.title: Producer deployed before its consumer
classes.signature: A new message kind, template or enum value is emitted while an old consumer is still running during a rollout; the old one drops it as unknown and the producer marks it done.
classes.question: During a rolling deploy, the old consumer receives the new message: does it fail, drop it, or leave it to retry?
